scheme_name: National Urban Sanitation Policy Innovation Challenge
overview: The National Urban Sanitation Policy Innovation Challenge is a scheme under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs aimed at fostering innovation in urban sanitation and waste management. It encourages stakeholders to develop and implement novel solutions for improving sanitation infrastructure and services in urban areas. The initiative supports the broader goals of the Swachh Bharat Mission and sustainable urban development by promoting technological and behavioral innovations.
objectives: Promote innovative solutions in urban sanitation and waste management
Encourage participation from startups, entrepreneurs, and local bodies
Support scalable and sustainable models for sanitation improvement
Strengthen the implementation of Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0
Foster public-private partnerships in urban service delivery
Enhance capacity building and knowledge sharing in sanitation sector
eligibility: Open to startups, entrepreneurs, MSMEs, urban local bodies, and other entities working on innovative solutions in urban sanitation, waste management, and related sectors. Applicants must demonstrate novelty, feasibility, and potential for scale in their proposed innovations.
benefits: Selected innovators receive recognition, mentorship, pilot implementation support, and potential scaling opportunities. The scheme facilitates access to funding networks, technical guidance, and visibility through MoHUA platforms. Non-financial benefits include capacity building, networking with policymakers, and integration into national urban missions.
financial_support: Financial support is provided through grants or seed funding for pilot projects, with amounts determined based on project scope and viability. The fund is leveraged to attract additional investment from private and public sources. Disbursement is linked to milestone achievement and project progress.
application_process: 1. Visit the official MoHUA website or designated portal for the Innovation Challenge. 2. Register and create a profile on the application portal. 3. Submit a detailed proposal outlining the innovation, objectives, methodology, and expected impact. 4. Upload supporting documents such as team details, prototypes, and pilot results. 5. Submit the application for review by the expert committee. 6. Await evaluation and notification of results.
required_documents: Proof of concept or prototype details
implementing_agency: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
caveats: Funding is subject to availability and project evaluation
Intellectual property rights remain with the innovator unless otherwise agreed
Continued support is contingent on performance and milestones
The scheme may be modified or discontinued based on policy updates
